commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary QuickTime tag buffer growth

The decoder only needs the four-byte box type. Avoid resizing the tag buffer to the payload size and construct the recursive tag name with an explicit length.

coupling: The first edited commit removes the one-byte NUL sentinel from the four-byte QuickTime box-type buffer and keeps recursion safe by constructing the tag name with an explicit length of four. The later edited commit changes that bounded construction to a std::string from buf.c_data(), which relies on a NUL terminator. Read alone, the later change is safe against the real first commit because that buffer is five bytes and explicitly NUL-terminated; read alone, the first change is safe because it uses an explicit length. Only their composition leaves a four-byte DataBuf consumed by a strlen-based std::string constructor, causing a heap out-of-bounds read when a valid QuickTime file contains a meta container. A correct fix must reason across both commits and coordinate the buffer capacity/terminator invariant with the string conversion; changing only one commit's diff leaves the mismatch reachable.
